title: Prior-session outlier basket reversal: USD-factor-neutral top-2 vs bottom-2 demeaned-return baskets
economic_mechanism: Yesterday's cross-sectional outliers among the seven majors - the pairs whose demeaned, USD-factor-neutral session returns were most extreme - systematically underperform today relative to yesterday's cross-sectional middle. The driver is liquidity provision: one-sided flow into yesterday's winning (USD-view) pair leaves dealers and fast money with inventory whose passive unwinding, plus renewed two-sided flow the next London session, pushes the outlier pair back toward the bloc norm. This is a short-horizon CROSS-SECTIONAL REVERSAL of demeaned returns - an inter-day effect measured and traded across the full 7-pair universe symmetrically (bottom-k basket vs top-k basket, k=2, by one frozen ranking rule) - not an intraday dislocation of a same-day extreme pair and not a single-pair signal.
causal_prediction: Conditional on yesterday's standardized demeaned session-return range being at least 2.0, today's bottom-2-minus-top-2 demeaned basket spread is positive on average and must clear 12.0 bps per round trip at the base cost tier (4 legs x 2 sides x 1.5 bps). A stale-ranking control (yesterday's ranking replaced by the T-2 ranking, all else identical) must NOT reproduce the effect, because two-day-old outliers are not what today's flow is unwinding; a trailing-8h-of-prior-session neighbour must move together with the anchor if reversal of recent outlier flow, rather than the exact full-session window, is the mechanism.

primary_literature_trace.citation: Lehmann, B. N. (1990), 'Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency', Quarterly Journal of Economics 105(1)
primary_literature_trace.claim: Cross-sectional contrarian strategies that sell past short-horizon winners and buy past losers earn significant abnormal returns - short-horizon cross-sectional reversal is a large, robust empirical regularity, which this proposal ports to the demeaned cross-section of FX majors at the intraday-holdable horizon.

primary_literature_trace.citation: Nagel, S. (2012), 'Evaporating Liquidity', Review of Financial Studies 25(7)
primary_literature_trace.claim: Short-term reversal returns are compensation for providing liquidity when other investors demand it, spiking when liquidity evaporates - the economic rationale for why yesterday's flow-driven outliers partially revert when two-sided liquidity returns the next session.

h1_observables: completed H1 bar open and close prices (bar-open UTC timestamps) for all 7 pairs; log increments only

prior trading day's usd_view session return per pair: s_p * (log C_p(last completed bar with open strictly before the 16:00 America/New_York instant) - log O_p(first bar of that trading day)), trading days NY-rollover anchored
cross-sectional mean and demeaned residual of prior-session returns across the 7 pairs
trailing 20-trading-day rolling standard deviation of the same prior-session residual, per pair
no high/low, no volume, no D1 data, no bid/ask - open and close of completed H1 bars only

pit_timing.decision: decision bar = the H1 bar with open-time 07:00:00Z; the decision uses only that bar's close and earlier completed bars (the T-1 session is fully completed by 00:00Z, so the entire signal is known at the latest by 08:00:00Z)
pit_timing.entry: next allowed H1 bar open after decision-bar completion = the 08:00:00Z bar open; one-event lag, no lookahead; if any required bar is missing (any pair, current or trailing windows), the day is NO_DECISION -> NO_TRADE, never fill-forward
pit_timing.monitoring_and_exit: hold-to-flat: no intermediate exit exists; the only exit is the forced-flat fill
pit_timing.forced_flat_fallback: if the forced-flat bar is missing for a held pair, the exit fills at the first available later H1 bar open the same UTC day and the event is logged as FAIL_LATE_FILL

pair_universe.orientation_note: u_p = s_p * prior-session log-increment of the quoted pair price; positive u_p means USD strengthened vs that currency
pair_universe.symmetry: the bottom-k and top-k baskets are selected each day by one frozen ranking rule over all 7 pairs; no pair is privileged by name

usd_factor_neutral_construction.usd_index: m = (1/7) * sum_p u_p over the prior session (equal-weighted USD-strength index)
usd_factor_neutral_construction.standardization: z_p = e_p / sigma_p with sigma_p the trailing 20-trading-day std of the prior-session residual for pair p (requires >= 16 of the 20 trailing sessions valid, else NO_DECISION)
usd_factor_neutral_construction.trade_algebra: basket L = 2 pairs with the most negative z (usd_view long, x=+1 each); basket S = 2 pairs with the most positive z (usd_view short, x=-1 each); equal 1-unit notional per leg. Portfolio log return ~= sum_p x_p u_p = sum_p x_p e_p + m * (sum_L x - sum_S |x|) = sum_p x_p e_p because long and short units balance (2 vs 2). The equal-weighted USD index m cancels EXACTLY to first order, independent of which pairs the ranking selects.
usd_factor_neutral_construction.quoted_position_mapping: quoted-units position q_p = s_p * x_p (e.g. GBP/USD with x=+1 -> short GBP/USD spot; USD/CAD with x=-1 -> short USD/CAD spot)
usd_factor_neutral_construction.honesty_note: neutrality is w.r.t. the equal-weighted 7-pair USD proxy only; convexity and unequal per-currency volatilities are not neutralized; a Stage-A check must reject the explanation that plain USD drift (m) drives the anchor, since m cancels algebraically

clocks.warmup_note: 600 H1 bars (~25 trading days) covers the 20-day sigma window (20 x ~23 bars) plus one full prior session; all signal clocks frozen in UTC; only the forced-flat boundary is New-York anchored via zoneinfo
clocks.entry: 08:00:00Z bar open (next allowed H1 open after decision-bar completion)
clocks.exit_rule: hold-to-flat: no conditional exit; all 4 legs exit together at the forced-flat instant; zero intermediate parameters
clocks.forced_flat: exit at 16:00 America/New_York bar open on entry UTC day (20:00Z during EDT, 21:00Z during EST), strictly before the 17:00 NY rollover; no position crosses rollover
clocks.tier2_delay_interaction: the stress-tier 2.0 one-event delay applies to the entry and the single exit fill; the forced-flat boundary dominates and a delayed exit never crosses the 16:00 NY bar open

anchor.spec: one decision per UTC day at the 07:00Z-bar completion; rank the 7 pairs by standardized prior-session demeaned return z_p; gate: trade only if z_top1 - z_bot1 >= 2.0 (frozen constant); long the bottom-2 basket vs short the top-2 basket, 1 unit notional per leg, usd_view orientation; hold-to-flat exit at the 16:00 NY bar open
anchor.weekly_cap_backstop: schedule-level and PIT: a pair that has already made 3 round trips in the current Monday-anchored UTC week is skipped and replaced by the next pair in the frozen ranking order on the same tail; if fewer than 4 eligible pairs remain, NO_TRADE that day; guarantees <= 3 RT/pair/week and <= 1 entry/pair/UTC-day (the 4 selected pairs are always distinct)

neighbour.presumption_under_test: that the FULL prior session is the right reversal measurement window
neighbour.spec: identical anchor in every respect except u_p (and hence m, e, z, sigma) is measured over the FINAL 8 completed H1 bars of the prior trading day (the prior New York morning-and-afternoon segment) instead of the full session; same 2.0 gate, same bottom-2/top-2 baskets, same hold-to-flat exit
neighbour.expected_relation: should move TOGETHER with the anchor (correlated sign, similar or smaller magnitude) if reversal of recent outlier flow is the mechanism; divergence indicates a full-session-specific artifact

control.spec: identical anchor mechanics, gate, baskets, cost and exits, but the ranking is computed from the T-2 (two-trading-days-old) session return instead of the T-1 session; sigma standardization and the gate evaluation are unchanged and use the same trailing windows
control.expected_relation: must NOT reproduce the anchor: two-day-old outliers are de-linked from today's inventory unwinding while preserving trade count, leg count, cost and schedule; a positive stale-ranking expectancy would void the reversal mechanism claim

cost.per_leg_accounting: 4 legs (2 long + 2 short), each charged 1.5 bps x tier per side, entry and exit = 8 side-leg charges per round trip: 12.0 / 18.0 / 24.0 bps per round trip at tiers 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0; notional 10000 USD-unit per leg; counted honestly, never averaged away
cost.break_even_diagnostic: per-trade gross bps = 10^4 * mean(signed leg log-returns from the entry fill to the forced-flat fill, usd_view orientation); empirical per-side-per-leg break-even C* = mean gross bps / 8; PASS requires C* > 1.5 at base tier and C* > 3.0 at the tier-2.0 variant including its extra fill delay; the distribution of per-trade gross is reported, not only the mean

expected_frequency.analytic_estimate: gate P(z-range >= 2.0) over approximately standard normal demeaned session residuals is roughly 0.6-0.8; expected ~3.5 round trips per week across the whole construction (at most 1 per UTC day), each of 4 distinct pairs
expected_frequency.per_pair: expected ~3.5 x 4/7 = 2.0 RT/pair/week; hard schedule bounds: <= 1 entry/pair/UTC-day by construction (4 distinct pairs per day) and <= 3 RT/pair/week enforced by the frozen substitution backstop
expected_frequency.cost_feasibility_statement: the 4-leg construction must clear 12.0 bps gross per round trip at base tier; typical prior-session top2-bottom2 demeaned spreads are of order 50-120 bps, so reversal capture must exceed roughly 10-25% of the entry spread - this is the honest a priori hurdle and the proposal is designed to be judged against it, not against a reduced cost

folds_plan.rule: post-warmup decision UTC days are split into 3 equal contiguous chronological thirds (floor; remainder to the last fold); each trade belongs to the fold of its entry UTC day; positions are strictly intraday so no trade spans a fold boundary

concentration_plan.schedule_audit: no pair may exceed 50% of total round trips over the full sample; per-foreign-currency (EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, NZD, CHF, CAD) leg-count share reported with 50% audit limit; cash/account currency excluded
concentration_plan.scored_gate_input: per-pair share of gross positive PnL frozen at 40% limit for the Stage-A concentration gate

drop_one_pair_plan.rule: with any single pair excluded, recompute m as the 6-pair equal-weighted mean, e and sigma over the remaining 6, and re-run the same bottom-2/top-2 rule, gate, hold-to-flat exit and substitution backstop unchanged
drop_one_pair_plan.degradation_statement: the construction remains defined for all 7 single exclusions (k=2 of 6 is well-posed); USD neutrality then holds w.r.t. the 6-pair index and the excluded currency becomes unhedged - a documented degradation, not a failure

failure_interpretation.anchor_expectancy_nonpositive: inter-day cross-sectional outlier reversal is not exploitable net of 12 bps round-trip cost at any tier; reject the mechanism without cost rescue
failure_interpretation.control_reproduces: the apparent edge is not driven by yesterday's outliers - it would be a slow mean-reversion or schedule artifact; the reversal mechanism claim is void regardless of anchor sign
failure_interpretation.neighbour_diverges: the effect is specific to the full-session window; treat the anchor as window-specific and non-robust
failure_interpretation.break_even_below_base: if C* <= 1.5 bps per side per leg the 4-leg design is cost-infeasible as frozen; reject without re-design
failure_interpretation.usd_drift_explanation: if the scored USD-factor diagnostic shows the anchor's PnL is explained by m (which the algebra cancels only to first order), the neutrality claim fails and the proposal is rejected
failure_interpretation.frequency_violation: any realised schedule breaching <= 1 entry/pair/UTC-day or <= 3 RT/pair/week fails the preregistered contract outright

outcome_blind_attestation.statement: This proposal was designed solely from the frozen V2 contracts, the forbidden-family inventory and the session/calendar/schema modules. Every number above is a frozen constant chosen a priori; no grid, menu, range or result-aware choice exists in this file.
